_source: computed from the expert gold of the dev case (190 requirements, 4 regulations); rules are generic, no product text
_note: Use as shape rules for a synthetic expected.json. Numbers are targets, +-25% is fine.

per_regulation.note: one regulation (the product's own device regulation) 30-35% of the total, the rest spread 17-30% each

counts.paragraph_multiplicity: 87 of 121 paragraphs hold 1 requirement, 19 hold 2, 8 hold 3, a few hold 4-10 (long enumerations and parameter lists)

regulation_choice: Cite the consolidated / newest regulation for a topic, never one it supersedes, even when the product description mentions the older device type or the older regulation number.

Include the vehicle-installation regulation, the device-performance regulation(s) for each light/device the product is, and the device-marking/approval regulation if the product is a type-approved part.

Include a horizontal regulation (e.g. electromagnetic compatibility) when the product contains electronics (LED modules, a PCB, a controller), although no product-specific regulation cites it by number.
Leave out regulations about product kinds that are not present (other lamp functions, other vehicle categories, systems the product does not have).

section_mix.function_named_sections: 26% of requirements: sections named after a part or function of the product (installation rules, photometry/shape of the function the product performs)
section_mix.markings: 17%: approval-mark, identification and marking rules of the device
section_mix.general_and_emc_specifications: 44%: general specifications of the device, design/construction, electronic immunity and emission limits, mechanical/colour/material demands that apply because the product is a device, an electronic assembly or a plastic part; many of them are never named in the product description
section_mix.test_annex_methods: 12%: test-method annexes (weathering, thermal, ageing, photometric measuring conditions, sample numbers, tolerances), only the parameter lines that fix a condition, limit or sample count

include: Obligations that bind the product, its design, its marking, its performance or its installation.
Test-procedure parameters that fix a product condition (temperature, duration, test level, number of samples, tolerance) as a standalone requirement of the product or test sample.
Conditional obligations (When / Where / For ...) with the condition kept inside the requirement.
Obligations of the manufacturer that concern the product itself (e.g. what a marking must contain, how a sample must be supplied).
exclude: Administrative and application paperwork (how to apply for approval, documents to submit, communication of approvals, conformity of production procedures), and duties of type-approval authorities and technical services.
Definitions, scope statements, transitional provisions, explanatory notes and pure cross-reference sentences with no obligation of their own.
Requirements for variants the product is not: in a table keep only the row(s) for the product's own variant (e.g. its colour, class, category), not the other rows.
Obligations that are only permissions or options for something the product does not have.

requirement_form.style: Verbatim or near-verbatim sentence of the regulation, standalone (cross-references like 'paragraph 5.1.7.' are kept as in the source), numbers and units kept exactly. A list item is its own requirement with the lead-in sentence repeated or merged into it.

citation.paragraph_depth: mostly 3-4 levels deep (e.g. 6.10.4.2): 44% depth 3, 33% depth 2, 14% depth 1, ~6% depth 4+, ~4% top-level; annex items look like 'Annex 6 Part 6 3. Table A6-1'
citation.note: paragraph is the numbered paragraph the sentence sits in; page is the page of the PDF the paragraph starts on; the cited paragraph exists in the regulation text.
